jess_support: Heads-up — enterprise customer (acct: AC-992) reporting intermittent 422s on tool calls. They say it happens ~1/10 requests and usually when they call the `TranslateText` tool. They included a curl repro and request-id.

alan_engineer: Can you paste the curl + response and the exact tool handle they used? 422 means schema validation, but if body looks fine maybe wrong tool was selected.

jess_support: Here's the curl they used (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' 
 -d '{"tool":"TranslateText","args":{"text":"hello","target_lang":"es"}}'
```
Response (intermittent): HTTP 422
```
{"error":"schema_validation_failed","details":"expected tool schema for 'translatetext' but got args for 'translate_text'"}
```
Request-id: rid=0b3a-9f2c

maria_runtime: Hmm that error string is odd — it shows the service resolved the tool to a different canonical name (`translatetext`) than client sent (`TranslateText`). Could be a registry alias mismatch or case-normalization issue. Any recent registry deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy finished: registry-service v2026.10.2 by @eng_runtime at 2026-03-15T22:12:05Z :rocket: (rolling update)

alan_engineer: Would like the server-side logs for rid=0b3a-9f2c, and a stack trace if available. Also what region/customer tier? Dedicated or hosted?

jess_support: Hosted (prod-us-east). Attached logs from customer timeline (we redacted PII). Here are lines around the request: 
```
2026-03-16T03:44:10.123Z INFO tool_lookup request_id=0b3a-9f2c name="TranslateText" -> lookup result: alias="translateText" canonical="translatetext" match_type=alias
2026-03-16T03:44:10.124Z INFO router select_model request_id=0b3a-9f2c model=redwood-bert-1
2026-03-16T03:44:10.130Z WARN validation request_id=0b3a-9f2c schema_mismatch expected_schema="translate_text.v1" got_args_schema="translateText.v1"
2026-03-16T03:44:10.131Z ERROR toolcall request_id=0b3a-9f2c upstream_error=422
```

tony_oncall: That log suggests the registry returned an alias with different casing (`translateText`) but canonical lowercased name is `translatetext`. We should confirm whether lookup is performing case-sensitive matches and whether normalization changed during last deploy. Maria, can you check registry-sync job logs?

maria_runtime: Checking. The registry sync job (syncer) had a crash loop on one replica during the v2026.10 rollout. Found this in syncer logs: 
```
2026-03-15T22:11:58Z ERROR syncer: failed to apply alias mapping for model_id=mdl-778: key normalization mismatch: "TranslateText" != "translateText"
2026-03-15T22:12:00Z INFO syncer: partial apply succeeded on replica 1, replica 2 backoff
```
Looks like one replica applied the new alias mapping while another had old normalization logic, leading to a window where different API servers had different alias-to-canonical mappings.

alan_engineer: That explains the intermittent nature. Traffic hitting a server with the old mapping got the old canonical and schema, leading to validation mismatch. Two action items: 1) roll a quick patch to make lookup case-insensitive fallback, 2) run a one-off reconciliation to re-apply canonical aliases across all replicas and mark them consistent.

jess_support: Customer is impacted and wants ETA + mitigation. They asked if temporary workaround exists on client side.

eng_runtime: Client workaround — normalize tool names to lowercase before sending (e.g., `translatetext`) — will avoid mismatch while we fix server. We'll also push a hotfix to registry-service to normalize aliases on read and write. ETA for reconciliation + hotfix: ~90 minutes.

tony_oncall: I'm going to schedule an urgent reconciliation job and pin it to low-traffic window. Will also add a short-lived rate-limit to shard hitting the older replica until sync completes.

jess_support: Sent customer the workaround (lowercase handle) and offered 5k token credit for the incidents. Customer accepted provisional workaround but asked for postmortem.

maria_runtime: After reconciliation: all replicas report alias mapping consistent. Added extra acceptance test to CI that asserts case-insensitive alias resolution. Also added a healthcheck that fails if any replica reports >0 mismatches.

alan_engineer: Deployed patch v2026.10.3 that adds case-insensitive fallback and stronger normalization on write. Monitoring shows errors drop to 0. Rolling back rate-limit.

jess_support: Customer confirmed errors stopped. Leaving for postmortem writeup. Closing escalation unless anyone objects. :thumbsup:

eng_runtime: Filing postmortem doc and linking to this thread. We'll include repro, timeline, root cause (partial sync during deploy + normalization mismatch), mitigation (client normalization + server hotfix), ongoing work (CI test + healthcheck).

tony_oncall: Recommended follow-ups: add canary gating for registry-schema changes and add a pre-deploy check that all syncer replicas are at parity before flipping traffic.

jess_support: Thanks everyone — marked as resolved with actions for follow-up.
